content: We have carbon NMR shifts list. Need number of CH3 groups (methyl). Identify which carbon signals correspond to methyl carbons. Typically methyl carbon chemical shift around 10-30 ppm for aliphatic, maybe 15-30. In list we have 19.23 ppm likely a methyl. Also 52.24, 49.55, 43.55 are likely carbons attached to heteroatoms (e.g., O, N). 166.40 carbonyl, aromatic around 144-127. So only one methyl at 19.23. Could there be other methyls hidden? 52.24 could be O-CH3 (methoxy) shift ~55 ppm, also methyl. So that is also a CH3. So we have two methyl groups: one aliphatic (19.23) and one methoxy (52.24). Need to decide based on typical shift ranges. Retrieve carbon shift ranges to confirm.
